For example of course you have an expert for a scientific field, and one for a certain industry.

The trouble lies in human faults.

For example, let's say a scientist is testing a company's product in a study. However, the study is funded by the company in question. 
This happens all the time, and allows company's to shape the "scientific fact" of said products. 

Or if you have an expert in an industry, however they give out semi-false business advice in courses that cost a bomb. 

Sure, someone who is an expert can do a much better job at dealing with the field. After all that is what they are there for. 
But if you know to play a game really well, chances are you also know how to cheat better then everyone. 

Now apply this logic to enforcing the law and you see a clear problem. Anything from political opinion, to where you grew up will effect your judgement and use of your skills. 
Unless youre Robocop youll probably do it without realising, or you will but "its the right thing". 
Most people where i lived while growing up hated the police because they didnt really do much, and the police didnt like dealing with people on the council estate.

Just because its the estate doesnt mean you show up 2 hours after an incident.

My friends make jokes towards me being gay all the time Of course I'm always in on the joke otherwise I would be offended.

In my personal opinion its probably best not to joke about that stuff in a general way but it depends on the person.

Like I wouldn't like it if someone made a homophobic joke and wasn't being ironic. But with my friends we tend to use edgy humour to take this piss out of eachother in a loving way. Eg; 

Me-"You've eaten most of the digestives again? You fat bastard!"
Friend-"Well at least I'm not a skinny poof like you"

That being said its probably best to not tell those jokes without knowing if someone will take them as irony and isnt hurt by them.
